subject: AI & Agents
title: Open Source vs Closed Models
description: A 60-second lesson on Open Source vs Closed Models.

hook.text: Meta releases Llama for free. OpenAI keeps GPT-4's weights locked. Both strategies have merit.

buildup.text: Open-source models let anyone inspect, modify, and deploy them. Closed models are API-only.

discovery.text: Open models drive research, customization, and privacy. Closed models lead in raw capability.

twist.text: Open models can be fine-tuned to remove safety guardrails — a double-edged sword.

climax.text: The open-source community is closing the gap fast. Llama 3 rivals GPT-3.5 in many tasks.

punchline.text: The best model depends on what you need: power or freedom.

quiz.question: What is a risk of open-source AI models?
options: They can be modified to remove safety guardrails
They are always less capable than closed models
They can only run on specific hardware

details.summary: Open-source LLMs like Llama and Mistral are freely available for anyone to use, modify, and deploy. Closed models like GPT-4 are only accessible via paid APIs. This divide shapes AI's future accessibility and innovation.
details.whyItMatters: Whether AI is open or closed determines who can build with it, inspect it, and benefit from it. This is a defining question for whether AI power concentrates or distributes across society.
takeaways: Open-source models are free to download, modify, and self-host
Closed models offer more capability but lock users to one provider
The open vs closed debate shapes AI's future power structure

faq.question: What are the best open-source language models?
faq.answer: Meta's Llama 3, Mistral's models, and Google's Gemma are leading open-source LLMs. They approach closed model performance on many tasks while allowing full customization and private deployment.

faq.question: Why would a company choose open-source over closed models?
faq.answer: Data privacy (no data sent to third parties), customization through fine-tuning, no per-token API costs at scale, no vendor lock-in, and the ability to deploy anywhere including offline environments.
